{{Western name order|Hiyama Emiko}}
'''Emiko Hiyama''' ({{langx|ja|肥山 詠美子}}) is a Japanese computational [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] whose research concerns computational methods for [[few-body systems]] of nucleons.{{r|aiming}} She is the director of the Strangeness Nuclear Physics Laboratory at the [[Riken]] Nishina Center for Accelerator-Based Science,{{r|riken}} and a professor of physics at [[Tohoku University]].{{r|tohoku}}

==Education and career==
Hiyama is originally from [[Fukuoka Prefecture]],{{r|tohoku}} and studied physics at [[Kyushu University]].{{r|researchmap}}

She was a researcher for [[KEK]], the Japanese High Energy Accelerator Research Organization, from 2000 to 2004. In 2004, she became an associate professor at [[Nara Women's University]]. She moved to Riken in 2008, and became laboratory director there in 2018. From 2017 to 2020 she was also affiliated with the Department of Physics at [[Kyushu University]], and in 2021 she took her present position as a professor at [[Tohoku University]].{{r|researchmap}}

==Recognition==
Hiyama was the 2013 winner of the [[Saruhashi Prize]],{{r|saru1}} for "developing computational methods for precise solutions of quantum <math>n</math>-body problems".{{r|saru2}}
